title: Quantized FlashAttention routing & prefill latency delta analysis
creator: Liang Chen
description: Summary: A recent rollout of quantized FlashAttention v3 kernels (qFA3) for T5-like models shows a measurable prefill tail-latency increase for many short-lived requests. This ticket investigates the root causes, verifies interactions with routing heuristics, and proposes targeted mitigations.
background: We enabled qFA3 as a low-memory, high-throughput kernel on the inference fleet for model: redwood/t5-xl-quant. Telemetry after the rollout (2025-02-10) shows 95th/99th percentile prefill latency increased by ~18% and ~34% respectively for <64-token requests in the hosted tier. Total token cost per request is unchanged. Initial correlation points to more frequent kernel switch events and KV-cache churn during short sessions.
hypothesis: 1) The qFA3 kernel has different startup scheduling characteristics (smaller subkernel tiling) that make very short prefill sequences less cache-friendly. 2) Smart-routing policy intermittently routes identical short requests between qFA3 and legacy qFA2 based on transient capacity signals, causing more KV cache warming and cross-kernel reconstructions. 3) Quantized memory layout differences trigger extra memcpy/transpose paths in the runtime for some model shapes, adding latency for prefill but amortizing well during long decodes.
diagnostics_performed:
- End-to-end traces (token-level spans) of 5000 synthetic short requests and 2000 production traces with user opt-in: found 2.3x more kernel-init spans per request on qFA3 paths.
- Microbenchmarks on a single A100 instance comparing qFA2 vs qFA3 for seq_len 16/32/64: qFA3 shows slightly higher single-request prefill latency but superior steady-state throughput for batched long sequences.
- KV cache hit/miss histograms: increased warm misses when routing toggles kernels mid-session.
- Heap/memory profiler: observed additional 8-12KB transient buffers allocated when qFA3 path converts quantized tensors for attention kernels.
findings:
- Kernel selection log shows policy thresholds that prefer qFA3 when estimated memory headroom > 20% and expected decode length > 128 tokens; however, the estimator uses a FIFO capacity signal that can flip for bursty traffic, causing oscillation for short sessions.
- The runtime performs a lightweight quant-layout rewrite when switching between qFA2 and qFA3; this step adds ~0.9-1.6ms per switch on average.
- Prefill (encoder-like) paths are more sensitive to these layout rewrites because they occur before any caching can amortize the cost.
- No correctness regressions found in output; quality metrics and log-likelihoods are unchanged within noise.
mitigation_options:
1) Stabilize routing: add a sticky routing window (e.g., 30s) per client token to avoid oscillation between qFA variants. 2) Lazy layout conversion: defer quant-layout rewrite until decode start for short prefill-only requests; skip if expected decode length < 64. 3) Micro-optimization: merge memcpy+transpose into single CUDA kernel to remove the 0.9-1.6ms penalty. 4) Rollback: temporarily route short requests to qFA2 until mitigations land.
Each option traded off implementation effort vs. impact and rollback complexity.
selected_plan: Short term (hotfix): implement sticky routing window of 15s and a server-side guard to avoid converting layouts for prefill-only requests with expected_decode_len < 64. Long term: upstream optimized combined-copy kernel and refine capacity estimator to include sequence-length distribution predictions.
